headline: Organic growth hits a multi-year high as margins expand
summary_short: Applied Industrial Technologies' fiscal Q4 2026 (three months ended June 30, 2026) net sales rose 10.4% y/y to $1,352.7M (+8.1% q/q) on 9.7% organic growth — the strongest in three-plus years — with diluted EPS up 13.2% y/y to $3.17; the company introduced FY2027 guidance of $11.65-$12.15 EPS on 4.0%-6.5% sales growth.
summary_long: Organic growth of 9.7% was led by a 12.9% increase in Engineered Solutions and 7.9% in Service Center. EBITDA margin expanded over 60bp on steady gross margin and operating leverage, with EBITDA up 16.1% y/y to $177.6M; net income rose 10.0% y/y to $118.6M ($3.17 diluted EPS, +13.2% y/y), despite a larger LIFO drag ($6.4M vs $2.9M). Full-year net sales were $5.0B (+8.8%) and diluted EPS $10.95 (+8.2%). Applied introduced initial FY2027 guidance of $11.65-$12.15 EPS on 4.0%-6.5% sales growth and 12.5%-12.8% EBITDA margins, and raised intermediate targets to $7B sales, 14% EBITDA margin. Cash fell to $127.1M (-67.3% y/y) after $317.2M of buybacks and a $310M revolver repayment; long-term debt fell to $262.3M (-54.2% y/y).

drivers.explanation: CEO Schrimsher called it the strongest organic growth in three-plus years, citing differentiated technical positioning and sales initiatives against an increasingly favorable end-market backdrop, with EBITDA margin up over 60bp and mid-teens EBITDA/EPS/free-cash growth.
9.7% organic growth (12.9% Engineered Solutions, 7.9% Service Center) plus 0.3% from acquisitions and 0.4% FX tailwind drove the 10.4% reported increase.
Company cited steady gross margin performance alongside the sales increase; no specific mix or pricing detail was broken out for gross profit itself.
Combination of the reported sales increase and operating leverage the company attributes to margin expansion; SD&A grew slower (+5.1% y/y) than gross profit (+9.7% y/y).
Management attributes the >60bp EBITDA margin expansion to steady gross margin plus operating leverage on the higher sales base.
Revenue and operating-income growth outweighed a higher pre-tax LIFO expense drag ($6.4M vs $2.9M prior year) and a higher effective tax rate (24.8% vs 20.1% y/y).
EPS grew faster than net income (+13.2% vs +10.0% y/y) because diluted shares outstanding fell to 37.4M from 38.5M y/y on continued buybacks.
Cash fell as $711.5M of full-year financing outflows — $317.2M of treasury-share buybacks, a $310M revolving-credit repayment, and $72.6M of dividends — exceeded $484.1M of operating cash flow.
Debt declined on the $310M revolving-credit-facility repayment disclosed in the full-year financing activities.
Equity held roughly flat as $414.5M of full-year net income was largely offset by $317.2M of buybacks and $72.6M of dividends paid.
